articles.title: Indian Banks Just Doubled Dollar Deposit Rates for NRIs to 7%. The RBI Engineered It — and It Will Not Last.
articles.excerpt: After the RBI agreed on June 5 to absorb the full hedging cost on fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) dollar deposits, banks have lifted rates from around 3 per cent to between 5.25 and 7.1 per cent. With no currency risk, these are among the most attractive dollar-denominated returns NRIs have seen in years — but the concessional window slams shut on September 30, and the offer is dollar-only.
articles.image_caption: US dollar banknotes; Indian banks are offering NRIs up to 7.1 per cent on dollar FCNR(B) deposits
articles.nri_angle: FCNR(B) deposits are an NRI-only instrument, and the sudden jump to 6-7.1 per cent on a dollar deposit with zero currency risk — deliberately engineered by the RBI to pull diaspora dollars into India — is one of the most consequential, time-limited financial decisions facing NRI savers right now, with a hard September 30 deadline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Just Fell to a Six-Month Low — and JP Morgan Says It Is Heading to $6,000. For NRIs, the Dip Is the Story.
articles.excerpt: After a 64 per cent surge in 2025, gold has stalled, sliding below $4,022 an ounce this month and dragging Indian prices to a six-month low near ₹146,000 per 10 grams. JP Morgan still forecasts $6,000 by year-end. With India's 15 per cent import duty, a recovering rupee and the Iran peace deal all pulling in different directions, diaspora buyers face a genuine decision: is this the buying window, or the start of a longer cooling?
articles.image_caption: Gold bullion, the asset at the centre of diaspora wedding, festival and investment decisions
articles.nri_angle: Gold sits at the centre of NRI financial life — wedding gifting, festival buying, portfolio hedging and money sent home — and the collision of a sharp price correction, a bullish $6,000 forecast, India's steep 15 per cent import duty and a recovering rupee turns the next few weeks into a concrete timing decision for diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Niño Is Back, and India's Monsoon Has Started With a 26% Rain Deficit. Here Is What It Means for Markets and NRIs.
articles.excerpt: Just as oil's crash and the rupee's rally lifted sentiment, a freshly declared El Niño and a weak start to the monsoon — rainfall ran 26 per cent below normal in early June — have introduced the one risk that could derail India's recovery: the rains that half its farmland depends on. For NRIs eyeing Indian equities and rupee-denominated deposits, the monsoon is now the variable to watch.
articles.image_caption: A farmer in a flooded paddy field during the monsoon, the rains that half of India's farmland depends on
articles.nri_angle: A weak monsoon directly threatens the rural demand, food inflation and rupee stability that underpin NRI investments and the purchasing power of remittances sent home — making this year's El Niño-shadowed season a concrete factor in diaspora financial decisions, from equity exposure to the timing of money transfers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Largest Stock Exchange Is About to Go Public. The NSE's Mega-IPO Could Be the Country's Biggest Ever.
articles.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange is set to file its draft prospectus with SEBI this week for an offering structured entirely as a sale of existing shares, with its unlisted stock already valued above ₹5 lakh crore in the grey market. For NRIs who have long held NSE shares privately — and for those who want in — this is the moment a decade in the making.
articles.image_caption: A stock exchange trading environment, as India's NSE prepares its landmark public listing
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs and OCIs have held National Stock Exchange shares for years in the unlisted market, and a public listing finally offers a transparent exit and price discovery — while the broader opening of India's markets to foreign individuals makes the IPO a live opportunity for the diaspora rather than a spectator event.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Wholesale Inflation Just Hit a Six-Month High of 9.68%. Why the RBI Is Not Panicking — and What It Means for NRIs.
articles.excerpt: May wholesale price inflation came in far above forecasts at 9.68 per cent, driven by a 61 per cent surge in petroleum and gas prices from the Middle East energy shock. Yet retail inflation sits below 4 per cent and the rupee is rallying — a divergence diaspora investors and remittance senders need to understand.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes, as wholesale inflation climbed to a six-month high
articles.nri_angle: The gap between soaring wholesale prices and tame retail inflation, combined with a rallying rupee, directly shapes how far NRI remittances stretch and whether the Reserve Bank moves on rates — decisions that affect every diaspora family sending money home or invested in Indian assets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreigners Dumped ₹62,800 Crore of Indian Stocks This Month. Then the RBI Quietly Reopened the Debt Door.
articles.excerpt: As foreign portfolio investors pulled a record ₹2.87 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026, New Delhi scrapped taxes on government bonds and subsidised NRI deposit hedging — triggering over $1 billion of foreign bond buying in days and reshaping where diaspora money should look.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The RBI's package directly targets non-resident Indians — fully subsidising hedging costs on three-to-five-year NRI dollar deposits until September — while the bond-tax overhaul changes the risk-reward calculation for diaspora investors weighing Indian equities against fixed income.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kevin Warsh Takes the Chair at a Fed Nobody Agrees On. For NRI Investors, This Week Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: The new Fed chair's first meeting lands as inflation hits a three-year high, Iran peace sends oil tumbling, and the rupee claws back toward 94. The dot plot may already have shifted under him.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the White House, May 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors face a pivotal week: the Fed's rate path directly affects dollar deposit yields, rupee remittance math, and the attractiveness of Indian vs US equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Hit a New-Series High. For NRIs, the Real Number Is Much Worse.
articles.excerpt: Official CPI rose to 3.93% in May, but food inflation is at 4.78%, fuel prices have been hiked four times, and the RBI just raised its full-year forecast to 5.1%. Every rupee you send home now buys less than it did in January.
articles.image_caption: A government official briefs media on inflation — India's consumer price index has hit a new series high, with NRI purchasing power eroding faster (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI remittances are worth less in real terms as India's food and fuel inflation accelerates — the RBI's revised 5.1% forecast for FY27 means the purchasing power of every dollar sent home is eroding faster than at any point since the new CPI series launched.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Doubled Its Gold Tariff. Smugglers Are Making ₹25 Lakh Per Kilo Bar. NRIs Are Caught in the Middle.
articles.excerpt: The 15 per cent import duty was meant to defend the rupee. Instead it has fuelled a grey-market revival that could hit 100 tons this year — while JP Morgan forecasts $6,000 gold by December.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs buying gold for weddings or investment now face an 18.45 per cent embedded tax in India — reshaping how and where the diaspora acquires gold.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Below $86, Rupee at 95, Markets Up 2%. The Iran Peace Deal Could Reshape Every NRI Financial Calculation.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude plunged to a three-month low. The rupee posted its best single-day gain in weeks. Indian equities had their strongest session in two months. Here is what it means for your money.

articles.title: India's SIP Machine Has Grown Tenfold in a Decade. Equity Mutual Fund Flows Just Hit a One-Year Low. What NRIs Should Read Into Both.
articles.excerpt: Monthly SIP contributions surged from ₹3,189 crore to ₹30,954 crore in ten years even as foreign investors dumped a record $30 billion of Indian stocks in 2026.
articles.image_caption: Stock market trading screens displaying financial data and market movements
articles.nri_angle: NRIs deciding whether to stay invested in India face a structural shift: domestic SIP-driven capital now provides floor support that makes timing the market from abroad harder, while FCNR deposits offer a complementary low-risk dollar yield.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Have Fled 43 of India's 50 Biggest Stocks. Domestic Money Is Filling the Void.
articles.excerpt: FII ownership in Indian equities has plunged to a 14-year low of 14.7 per cent, while domestic institutional holdings have surged to a record 18.9 per cent — a structural shift that reshapes risk and opportunity for NRI investors.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — foreign institutional investors have pulled back from most of India's top 50 stocks
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors face a double bind: the record foreign exit from Indian equities has eroded returns in dollar terms, but the structural shift toward domestic ownership may reduce future volatility and create a more favourable entry point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s IT Stocks Have Lost 27 Per Cent This Year. For NRI Tech Workers, the Pain Is Doubly Personal.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has shed more than a quarter of its value in 2026 as AI disruption fears collide with macro headwinds. For the millions of Indian-origin professionals who work in the same industry they invest in, the exposure is uniquely concentrated.
articles.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displaying real-time financial data and price movements
articles.nri_angle: NRI tech workers often hold ESOPs in Indian IT firms, invest in IT-heavy mutual funds, and work in the very sector AI threatens to disrupt — creating a rare triple concentration of career, portfolio, and identity risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GIFT City Just Got Its First US Company Listing. Here Is What NRIs Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: Banking assets at $111 billion, US stocks now accessible, and the first American IPO on Indian exchanges — India's answer to Dubai and Singapore is crossing a threshold.
articles.image_caption: GIFT One tower in Gujarat — the centrepiece of India's first International Financial Services Centre
articles.nri_angle: GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient hub specifically for NRI wealth management, cross-border investing, and India-linked portfolios — a direct alternative to routing capital through Dubai or Singapore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened Its Stock Market to Every Foreigner on Earth. Here Is What Changed Overnight.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping FEMA amendment notified on June 12 replaces the NRI-only investment framework with one that lets any individual residing outside India buy and sell listed Indian equities — a historic shift in capital account liberalisation.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs already invested in Indian equities now share the playing field with every foreign individual globally — understanding the new rules, limits, and safeguards is essential to protect existing holdings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. Here Is How to Get the Best Rate Before September.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's unprecedented forex swap has sparked a rate war among banks. Emkay calculates leveraged returns could reach 22%. The window closes September 30.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn 6-7% on dollar deposits at Indian banks with zero currency risk before the RBI's concessional swap window closes September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. For NRI Investors, the Timing Could Not Be Better.
articles.excerpt: Tax exemptions, subsidised hedging, and a $3 billion corporate debt rush — India's most aggressive capital-market reforms in years are rewriting the playbook for overseas fixed-income investors, with Bloomberg index inclusion now weeks away from a decision.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building, headquarters of the central bank driving India's bond-market reforms
articles.nri_angle: NRI depositors benefit directly from RBI's fully subsidised hedging on foreign currency deposits, while the tax exemptions on government bonds make Indian fixed income a viable portfolio allocation for the first time in years — particularly for diaspora investors burned by the rupee's depreciation and looking for yield with policy support.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Nino Is Officially Here. India's Monsoon, Food Prices, and NRI Portfolios Are All in the Firing Line.
articles.excerpt: The US Climate Prediction Center and India's Met department have both confirmed moderate-to-strong El Nino conditions during the monsoon season — the first since 2023 and potentially one of the strongest on record. Here is what it means for your money.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity, bond, or commodity exposure face direct portfolio risk from El Nino through FMCG margin compression, rupee weakness, and potential RBI policy shifts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
